learning_outcomes.text: Be able to solve elasticity problems applying analytical and energetic methods.
Be able to solve strength of materials problems applying analytical and energetic methods.
Be able to explain, summarize and describe the experiments carried out in the laboratory and the conclusions and results derived from them.
Be able to pre-dimension structural and machinery elements from a mechanical point of view based on resistance, stiffness, and stability requirements.
Be able to calculate the stress and deformation state in systems composed of rod and beam elements subjected to axial, shear, bending, and torsional forces in isostatic and hyperstatic cases.
Know and understand the basic principles of plasticity in continuous media.
Understand and be able to apply the principles of elasticity in the analysis of the stress and deformation state of continuous media subjected to external actions.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to Failure and plastification criteria
Concept of failure and safety factor
Maximum Normal Stress or Rankine's Criterion
Maximum Shear Stress or Tresca's Criterion
Maximum Distortion Energy or Von Mises' Criterion
Adopted hypotheses in strength of materials
Relationship between forces and load distribution
Distribution of tangential stresses in solid circular section profiles
Distribution of tangential stresses in hollow circular section profiles
Formulation and resolution of Elasticity problems using Matlab / Octave software
Calculations of cross-sectional properties of beams
teaching_methods: Laboratory practical sessions using computer tools (spreadsheets, finite element software, mathematical calculation tools)

assessment_methods.method: Continuous assessment: Average of written theoretical/practical knowledge tests

assessment_rules: To pass the course, an overall grade of at least 5 out of 10 is required. In the first call, a minimum of 4.5 out of 10 must be obtained on the final exam to be able to average with continuous assessment; otherwise, the final grade will be solely the exam grade. In the second call, the final grade will be the maximum of Option A (Continuous Assessment 30% + Final Exam 70% with a minimum of 4.5) or Option B (Laboratory Reports 15% + Final Exam 85% with a minimum of 4.5). For the extraordinary end-of-studies call, the final exam accounts for 100% of the grade. Laboratory practical reports are not recoverable, but written theoretical/practical tests can be recovered in the second call's final exam.
